blocks.text: Imagine you are tasked with creating multiple types of vehicles in a simulation. Each vehicle has different attributes and behaviors. How can you efficiently manage their creation without cluttering your code?

blocks.markdown: Creational patterns are a category of design patterns that deal with object creation mechanisms. They aim to create objects in a manner suitable to the situation. The primary goal is to decouple the instantiation of objects from their usage, enhancing flexibility and reuse.

blocks.title: Factory Pattern
blocks.text: The Factory Pattern defines an interface for creating an object, but lets subclasses alter the type of objects that will be created.

blocks.markdown: The Factory Pattern is useful when the exact type of object to be created depends on dynamic conditions. It abstracts the instantiation process, allowing the client code to work with interfaces rather than concrete classes.

blocks.title: Factory Pattern Example
blocks.prompt: Implement a factory pattern to create different types of vehicles: Car and Truck.

steps.text: Define a Vehicle interface with a method `drive()`.
Create concrete classes Car and Truck implementing the Vehicle interface.
Implement a VehicleFactory class with a method `createVehicle(String type)` that returns a Vehicle.
In `createVehicle`, return a new Car or Truck instance based on the input type.

blocks.answer: The factory pattern allows us to create Car or Truck objects without exposing the instantiation logic to the client.

blocks.title: Builder Pattern
blocks.text: The Builder Pattern separates the construction of a complex object from its representation, allowing the same construction process to create different representations.

blocks.markdown: The Builder Pattern is particularly useful when an object needs to be constructed with many optional parameters, which can lead to long and confusing constructors.

blocks.title: Builder Pattern Example
blocks.prompt: Design a builder pattern for creating a House object with optional features like a garage, swimming pool, and garden.

steps.text: Define a House class with attributes for optional features.
Create a static nested Builder class inside House.
Provide methods in the Builder class to set optional features and a `build()` method to return a House instance.
Use the Builder to create a House with desired features.

blocks.answer: The builder pattern allows for a flexible and readable way to construct a House object with various optional features.

blocks.title: Singleton Pattern
blocks.text: The Singleton Pattern ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.

blocks.markdown: While the Singleton Pattern can be useful for managing shared resources, it has drawbacks such as hindering unit testing and introducing global state, which can lead to hidden dependencies.

blocks.title: Choosing Patterns
blocks.text: Choose a pattern based on the specific problem you are solving. Consider the trade-offs and ensure the pattern enhances the design.

points: Creational patterns manage object creation, enhancing flexibility.
The Factory Pattern abstracts instantiation, the Builder Pattern simplifies complex object creation, and the Singleton Pattern restricts a class to one instance.
Each pattern has specific use cases and drawbacks to consider.
